title: The Purified Ones And Verifying Scholars Proof Through Demonstrations

questions.question: After leaving the gathering of the prophets, where was the traveler invited next?
questions.answer: He was invited to the learning circle of pure and truthful scholars who support the prophets’ message with strong proofs.

questions.question: What kind of people were in that classroom?
questions.answer: It was filled with highly intelligent and careful scholars who studied matters of faith deeply.

questions.question: What were those scholars proving first and foremost?
questions.answer: They were proving that Allah truly exists and that He is One.

questions.question: How strong were their proofs described to be?
questions.answer: Their proofs were so solid and deep that they left no room for doubt.

questions.question: Why is their agreement important even though they differed from one another?
questions.answer: Because they had different abilities and viewpoints, yet still agreed on the main beliefs, which shows the truth is very strong.

questions.question: What does the passage say each scholar depended on?
questions.answer: Each one relied on firm and certain evidence.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would someone have to do to seriously challenge all those scholars?
questions.answer: He would have to show that many wise and sharp-minded people could all reach the same conclusion wrongly.

questions.question: How is the denier described if he rejects their united conclusion?
questions.answer: He is described as showing deep ignorance and stubbornness.

questions.question: What idea is taught by the example of a person shutting his eyes?
questions.answer: Refusing to see the truth does not change reality; it only darkens things for that person himself.

questions.question: For how long had the light of those scholars been spreading widely?
questions.answer: It had been shining over half the world for more than a thousand years.

questions.question: What kind of strength did the traveler find in that classroom?
questions.answer: He found spiritual and moral strength that people of denial could not overturn.

questions.question: What main lesson did the traveler gain from that classroom?
questions.answer: He learned that the united and certain proofs of purified scholars strongly point to Allah’s necessary existence and oneness.

questions.question: Why did the traveler feel drawn to the scholars after meeting the prophets?
questions.answer: Because he had tasted the truth through faith and was ready to learn from scholars who explained the prophets’ message with clear evidence.

questions.question: How are those scholars described in character and knowledge?
questions.answer: They are described as deep, original, careful, purified, and very truthful.

questions.question: What does the large number of scholars in the classroom suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the study and defense of faith is broad, serious, and supported by many great minds.

questions.question: Which parts of faith were they discussing?
questions.answer: They were discussing all the truths of belief, especially Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: What makes their agreement especially meaningful?
questions.answer: Their agreement matters even more because they were not all alike in skill or perspective, yet they still reached the same main conclusions.

questions.question: What does it show when different scholars use certain proofs and arrive at one result?
questions.answer: It shows that the result is trustworthy and not just a random opinion.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat denial of their conclusion as weak?
questions.answer: Because denial cannot stand against so many solid proofs and so much united scholarship.

questions.question: What is meant by saying some negative matters do not truly allow proper denial or affirmation in the way the denier acts?
questions.answer: It means the denier is not making a sound case but is only rejecting without real knowledge.

questions.question: What lesson about truth is taught by the image of day and night?
questions.answer: Truth stays clear like daylight even if someone personally refuses to admit it.

questions.question: What effect had these scholars had on the world?
questions.answer: Their teachings had enlightened a huge part of the world for over a millennium.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the scholars’ spiritual influence with the strength of deniers?
questions.answer: It says even all the deniers together could not shake or destroy that influence.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the central message of this passage?
questions.answer: The passage teaches that the united, certain, and long-lasting proofs of truthful scholars are a powerful witness to Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: What happened to the traveler after he benefited from the prophets’ gathering?
questions.answer: He was led to a class of truthful scholars who confirm the prophets’ teachings.

questions.question: What was special about the scholars’ way of defending belief?
questions.answer: They used the strongest and clearest proofs.

questions.question: About how many learned people did the traveler see there?
questions.answer: He saw thousands of brilliant minds and hundreds of thousands of precise and honored scholars.

questions.question: What were these scholars united on?
questions.answer: They were united on the foundations and main parts of faith.

questions.question: Did the passage say the scholars were identical in how they thought?
questions.answer: No, it says they differed in capacity and viewpoint.

questions.question: Why does their agreement despite those differences strengthen their case?
questions.answer: Because agreement among diverse thinkers shows the conclusion is based on truth, not copying or pressure.

questions.question: What supports each scholar’s position personally?
questions.answer: Each scholar has his own certain and firm proof.

questions.question: What would make doubt about all of them unreasonable?
questions.answer: Doubt would be unreasonable because so many intelligent and insightful people all reached the same result through proof.

questions.question: What moral problem is connected to rejecting their united witness?
questions.answer: The passage links it to stubborn refusal and serious ignorance.

questions.question: What does the image of closing one’s eyes teach about disbelief?
questions.answer: It teaches that disbelief cannot erase the truth; it only blinds the person who rejects it.

questions.question: What does the long spread of their light tell us about their work?
questions.answer: It tells us their teaching has had deep, lasting benefit across generations and lands.

questions.question: How would you summarize the traveler’s lesson from these scholars?
questions.answer: He learned that the agreement of purified scholars, backed by clear and certain proofs, is strong evidence for belief in Allah.

questions.question: What kind of “classroom” did the traveler enter in this passage?
questions.answer: He entered a figurative classroom made up of great scholars of faith.

questions.question: In relation to the prophets, what role did these scholars have?
questions.answer: They confirmed the prophets’ claims by giving powerful evidence.

questions.question: What two major beliefs are named as the leading subjects they proved?
questions.answer: Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: How certain were their demonstrations?
questions.answer: They were presented as so conclusive that no doubt was left.

questions.question: Why is the scholars’ shared belief counted as evidence by itself?
questions.answer: Because many wise and perceptive people agreeing on the same core truths points strongly to those truths.

questions.question: What kinds of differences existed among the scholars?
questions.answer: They differed in ability and in how they looked at things.

questions.question: Even with those differences, what remained the same?
questions.answer: Their agreement on the essentials of belief remained the same.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a denier really show by opposing them?
questions.answer: He shows ignorance and stubborn resistance.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the statement that someone can make night only for himself?
questions.answer: It means a person can hide the truth from his own mind, but he cannot change what is real.

questions.question: How far did the scholars’ light reach?
questions.answer: It reached half of the world.

questions.question: How long had that light been shining?
questions.answer: It had been shining for more than a thousand years.

questions.question: What final conclusion is highlighted in the brief summary at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: That the united agreement of purified scholars and their clear, certain proofs point to Allah alone.

questions.question: What inner change in the traveler led him into the scholars’ classroom?
questions.answer: His faith gave him a deep joy in truth, and that prepared him to seek stronger understanding.

questions.question: How are the scholars described besides being knowledgeable?
questions.answer: They are also described as sincere, refined, and very trustworthy.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of their work in that classroom?
questions.answer: Their purpose was to establish the truths of faith with decisive evidence.

questions.question: Why is it meaningful that there were both thousands and hundreds of thousands mentioned?
questions.answer: It emphasizes the great size, depth, and seriousness of the community defending belief.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the certainty of their evidence?
questions.answer: It says their evidence was dependable and gave certainty.

questions.question: How does diversity among the scholars make their agreement more convincing?
questions.answer: Since they came from different levels and perspectives, their agreement looks earned through truth rather than sameness.

questions.question: What challenge does the passage set for anyone who wants to doubt all of them?
questions.answer: The doubter would need to make it believable that a huge number of sharp and intelligent people all reached one conclusion incorrectly.

questions.question: How is blind rejection portrayed?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as an act of ignorance that harms only the rejecter.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the power of denial compared with the power of truth?
questions.answer: It teaches that denial is too weak to destroy truth that is supported by lasting, united proof.

questions.question: What had these scholars been doing for more than a millennium?
questions.answer: They had been spreading the light of faith and understanding across much of the earth.

questions.question: What kind of power did the traveler notice in their classroom that was not physical?
questions.answer: He noticed moral and spiritual power.

questions.question: What belief statement is affirmed in the concluding line of the target passage?
questions.answer: It affirms that there is no god but Allah and that the agreement of purified scholars supports this truth.

questions.question: Who welcomed the traveler after the assembly of the prophets?
questions.answer: A body of purified and truthful scholars welcomed him into their place of learning.

questions.question: What made these scholars important in the traveler’s journey?
questions.answer: They explained and defended the truths of faith with very strong arguments.

questions.question: What did the traveler observe when he entered their classroom?
questions.answer: He observed a vast number of brilliant scholars proving the matters of belief.

questions.question: Which belief comes first in the list of what they proved?
questions.answer: The first is that Allah necessarily exists and is One.

questions.question: What is one reason their consensus has great weight?
questions.answer: It has great weight because they all agreed on core beliefs even though they were not the same in thought and ability.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the basis of each scholar’s conclusion?
questions.answer: Each conclusion was built on solid and certain proof.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about doubting all of them at once?
questions.answer: It suggests that such doubt is unreasonable unless one could prove that many intelligent people can unite on one result without truth behind it.

questions.question: What does the passage say denial reveals about a person?
questions.answer: It reveals severe ignorance and stubbornness.

questions.question: How does the example of shutting one’s eyes help explain the denier’s condition?
questions.answer: It shows that rejecting truth does not erase it; it only leaves the rejecter in darkness.

questions.question: What long-term impact of these scholars impressed the traveler?
questions.answer: Their guidance had been lighting half the world for over a thousand years.

questions.question: Why could the people of denial not destroy what was in that classroom?
questions.answer: Because the classroom held a spiritual and moral strength stronger than all their combined efforts.

questions.question: What overall understanding did the traveler gain from this stage of his journey?
questions.answer: He understood that the shared and certain proofs of truthful scholars are a powerful witness to Allah’s necessary existence and unity.
